gaps.statement: Whether maternal prepregnancy obesity modifies SUID incidence differently across postconceptional age (PCA) windows has not been examined.
gaps.rationale: Maternal BMI is an established SUID risk factor in the literature, but neither manuscript included it. Estimating its association separately in the early rising (36-42 weeks) and late declining (>=47 weeks) PCA windows tests whether this risk is developmentally timed, extending the PCA framework to a new exposure.
gaps.prior_art: The literature abstracts report that maternal obesity raises SUID risk, increasing with BMI (suid_literature_abstracts.C10), without any developmental alignment. The PCA manuscript defined early and late PCA windows (SUID_manuscript_v9_clean.C5) but modelled sex and smoking, not maternal BMI.

gaps.statement: The joint effect of maternal smoking and preterm birth on SUID incidence across PCA windows has not been estimated.
gaps.rationale: Maternal smoking and prematurity are each strong, persistent correlates of SUID incidence across PCA, and prematurity is about twice as strong early as late. Whether smoking-associated risk differs between preterm and term infants within each PCA window is untested and bears on targeting prevention.
gaps.prior_art: The bed-sharing manuscript found maternal smoking the largest and most consistent correlate in both windows (bedsharing_ms_v7.C12) and prematurity positive throughout but stronger early (C13). Its interaction terms were bed sharing by smoking and bed sharing by preterm birth (C30); smoking by preterm birth was not estimated.

gaps.statement: Whether the rise-peak-decline pattern of SUID incidence by PCA differs across cause-of-death subtypes (SIDS R95, accidental suffocation and strangulation in bed W75, ill-defined R99) is unknown.
gaps.rationale: Certification of sudden infant deaths shifts between R95, R99 and W75 by certifier and circumstance. If the subtypes follow different PCA trajectories, the pooled SUID curve mixes distinct developmental patterns; if they share one trajectory, the pooled PCA finding is robust to the cause-of-death misclassification the PCA manuscript names as a limitation.
gaps.prior_art: The PCA manuscript found a clear rise, peak and decline in PCA-aligned SUID incidence (SUID_manuscript_v9_clean.C6) for R95, R99 and W75 pooled, and noted that vital-record data may misclassify cause of death (C12). Subtype-specific PCA trajectories were not reported.
